samples.summary: Design doc adds an `OAUTH_STATE_SECRET` env var (and an HKDF-of-`JWT_SECRET` default) that no code implements
samples.evidence: The diff adds `| \`OAUTH_STATE_SECRET\` | No | HKDF of \`JWT_SECRET\` | Key the OAuth login bindings are signed with…` to backend.md's environment table. Grepping `packages/backend/src` for `OAUTH_STATE_SECRET`, `hkdf`, `createHmac` and `process.env.JWT_SECRET` finds no such reading: `oauth-state.ts` mints web state as `randomBytes(32)` plus an unkeyed `createHash('sha256')` (`hashSecret`, oauth-state.ts:266), and the only HMAC added is `cliConfirmToken`, keyed by the confirm cookie secret, not by any configured key. The canonical subsystem doc therefore records a configuration knob and a signing scheme the branch does not have — an operator who sets it gets silence. Either implement it or drop the row.

samples.summary: The #661 `command` attribution is not applied to every emitter the design doc says it is: `status` and `ctx list` still emit an unattributed envelope

samples.summary: The change bundles four largely independent concerns into one branch
samples.evidence: Cookie `__Host-` prefixing + `COOKIE_SECURE` predicate (backend auth), CLI-login availability refusal and warning (backend guard), access-log URL/path redaction (new logging module), the CLI launch-token indirection and five-minute timeout (CLI login), and the #661 error-envelope attribution (CLI output) each have their own rationale and their own doc section. With no single originating issue covering all five, this is hard to review or revert as a unit; splitting along the doc sections it touches would fit the repo's per-area design-doc discipline better. Flagged as taste, not a blocker.

finding.summary: Design doc adds an `OAUTH_STATE_SECRET` env var (and an HKDF-of-`JWT_SECRET` default) that no code implements
finding.evidence: The diff adds `| \`OAUTH_STATE_SECRET\` | No | HKDF of \`JWT_SECRET\` | Key the OAuth login bindings are signed with…` to backend.md's environment table. Grepping `packages/backend/src` for `OAUTH_STATE_SECRET`, `hkdf`, `createHmac` and `process.env.JWT_SECRET` finds no such reading: `oauth-state.ts` mints web state as `randomBytes(32)` plus an unkeyed `createHash('sha256')` (`hashSecret`, oauth-state.ts:266), and the only HMAC added is `cliConfirmToken`, keyed by the confirm cookie secret, not by any configured key. The canonical subsystem doc therefore records a configuration knob and a signing scheme the branch does not have — an operator who sets it gets silence. Either implement it or drop the row.

verdict.reason: The finding is accurate as described. docs/design/backend.md:748 documents an `OAUTH_STATE_SECRET` env var with an "HKDF of JWT_SECRET" default and claims OAuth login bindings are "signed" with it; packages/backend/README.md:25-34 repeats this. No backend code implements it: a case-insensitive grep across packages/ for OAUTH_STATE_SECRET / STATE_SECRET / hkdf / createHmac finds no reader (only the cookie-name constant at oauth-state.ts:20 and error strings), and `process.env.JWT_SECRET`/`JWT_REFRESH_SECRET` appear nowhere in packages/backend/src. Web state is unkeyed: createWebOAuthState (oauth-state.ts:165-168) is randomBytes(32) plus createHash('sha256') via hashSecret (oauth-state.ts:266-268), verified by the same unkeyed hash in webOAuthStateMatches (oauth-state.ts:177-185). The only auth HMAC, cliConfirmToken (cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:97-107), is keyed by the confirm cookie secret, and its own comment at :90-92 says "there is no server key to configure or rotate" — directly contradicting the documented knob. So the canonical design doc records a configuration knob and signing scheme the branch does not have (silent no-op for an operator who sets it), a design-doc-accuracy/spec-conformance defect in this lens's lane and major in kind.

finding.summary: The #661 `command` attribution is not applied to every emitter the design doc says it is: `status` and `ctx list` still emit an unattributed envelope
finding.evidence: docs/design/cli.md §9 as rewritten by this diff asserts "Every emitter builds it in `packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts` — `outputError` for the throwing commands … so 'one line, attributed' holds on those too". Two `outputError` call sites were left without the acting command: `status.ts:69` (`outputError(e)`) and `ctx.ts:85` (`ctx list`, `outputError(e)`), which means an `INVALID_FORMAT` from `status` or a `NOT_LOGGED_IN` from `ctx list` still arrives with no `command` field while `ctx switch` now carries one — exactly the per-subcommand inconsistency the diff's own `ctx switch` comment argues against. Grep `outputError\((e|err|error)\)` over packages/cli/src returns only these two.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: an exhaustive grep of `outputError` over packages/cli/src shows every call site threading `this` EXCEPT `status.ts:69` and `ctx.ts:85` (`ctx list`), both of which sit inside `.action(function (this: Command) {…})` and therefore had the Command in scope. `outputError` (formatter.ts:158-163) computes `name = command ? commandPath(command) : ''` and `errorEnvelope` (formatter.ts:129-137) spreads `...(command ? {command} : {})`, so those two sites provably emit an envelope with no `command` field. No indirect attribution exists: the `preAction`-recorded `acting` command in cli.ts:80-99 only feeds runCli's last-resort catch, which these locally-caught throws never reach. Meanwhile `ctx switch` in the same file DOES attribute (ctx.ts:93,102-106,114), producing exactly the per-subcommand inconsistency its own comment argues against. Spec side: docs/design/cli.md:1492-1511 puts `command` in the envelope shape, claims "Every emitter builds it in packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts — outputError for the throwing commands", and names only `login` as the deliberate exception; the #661 todo's acceptance criterion (20260811-cli-error-envelope-command-todo.md:59-60) is "It carries `command` with the dotted command name", and its lessons file line 7 asserts the universal "all ~40 of them". Both documented matrix rows reachable here (INVALID_FORMAT from status.ts:64, NOT_LOGGED_IN from ctx.ts:79) emit unattributed. No test in packages/cli/test/output.test.ts covers or excepts these two. Unmet acceptance criterion + a design-doc universal claim falsified by the code = major under the design-fit rubric.
